text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 8.1% today, following a sharp 3.4% drop yesterday after the company reported quarterly earnings on November 3rd. The decline likely reflects disappointment in the company's forward guidance or operational outlook — refiners live and die by their profit margins, which compress when oil prices stay elevated but refined product prices don't keep pace. With US oil at $99.64 and the company's refineries running at 94.5% capacity, there's limited room for output growth to offset margin pressure.

The two-week, 16% selloff also tracks a broader caution about Big Oil earnings: investors were warned earlier this week that while headline earnings may look strong, the real question for refiner valuations is whether management can show sustainable profitability ahead. Rising oil inventories (692 million barrels in storage) and ample gasoline supply (209 million barrels) suggest demand may not be as robust as hoped, which would further squeeze refiner margins going forward.
